newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Market divided on D.Telekom as gag expires.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Market divided on D.Telekom as gag expires.

text.p: Stock analysts on Monday published a barrage of reports on German phone giant Deutsche Telekom AG as a regulatory gag rule expired, freeing analysts to comment on the share for the first time since its November listing.

As the first reports began to trickle into the market, analysts appeared to view the share as fair value at its current level of around 30 marks ($18.91) and saw some room for growth over the next six months, but there were few aggressive buyers.

The issue's three main underwriters -- Deutsche Bank AG, Dresdner Bank AG and U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs -- were divided in their recommendations with the German banks taking a much more positive view than their American counterpart.

Deutsche's investment arm Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) assigned Telekom a rating of "overweight", saying it would outperform the DAX index of 30 blue-chip stocks. Dresdner's Kleinwort Benson unit said to buy until shares hit 35 marks.

"We are initiating coverage with a recommendation of overweight," said James Golob, DMG telecommunications analyst. "If they can deliver compound growth as predicted then there will surely be room for capital appreciation."

James Riddiough, a Frankfurt-based DMG analyst, added: "By overweight, we mean that we believe it's going to outperform the DAX index." DMG predicted Telekom compounded net earnings would grow by 35 percent over the next five years.

But Goldman Sachs, reflecting earlier differences with its German partners over their valuation of Telekom shares, said it would initiate coverage of Deutsche Telekom with a rating of "market performer" and declined further comment.
Shares in Deutsche Telekom closed floor trade on Monday at 30.45 marks, down seven pfennigs from Friday, but still nearly seven percent above the initial offer price of 28.50 marks.
U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch started coverage of Telekom with a rating of near and long-term "accumulate".

Since its listing on November 18, when the company launched a $13 billion share offer and sold off more than 26 percent of its capital in Europe's largest stock listing ever, Telekom shares have underperformed the DAX index by around 16 percent.
The highest level Telekom shares have reached since closing at 33.90 marks on their first day of trade was 33.45 marks on November 29. They have been falling ever since.

Telekom shares have come under pressure for several reasons, analysts said. Lacking new information about its performance, there has been nothing to boost the stock after it fell from high levels of 33 marks and above in November.
That came as little surprise, as analysts across the board agreed that with the offer price at the high end of evaluations there was little room for near-term share price appreciation.
Investors are also anticipating the flotation of new shares by France Telecom and Spain's Telefonica, which are expected to issue some $9 billion in new stock later this year.
Commerzbank AG, Germany's third largest commercial bank, said it was keeping Telekom on "hold" and complained that the company had not made any recent comments on its business.
"There are no new data on the company," said analyst Sabine Schauer. "This is really astounding in the days of shareholder value and in light of the advertising hype ahead of the issue."
Schauer predicted Telekom shares would trade "sideways" in a range of 30-32 marks until 1996 earnings data were released.

This view was shared by Trinkaus Capital Management, which assigned an "underweight" rating to Telekom shares. Hamburg investment bank M.M. Warburg set a mid-term price target of up to 35 marks on Telekom shares and assigned a "hold" rating.

Bayerische Vereinsbank AG said it initiated coverage of Telekom with a rating as "outperformer". ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett assigned Telekom shares a rating of "undervalued" which one analyst said implied a recommendation to hold or buy.
Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel- Bank AG cut its rating on Telekom to "market performer" from "outperformer".
"The initial opportunity for share price gains was not seized by the market," said Bayernhypo analyst Roland Pitz. ($1=1.5865 Mark)
